text:
Jordan Lee: Hey team quick one – I tried accepting the GitHub org invite with `gh` (gh auth login + gh repo clone) but `gh orgs accept-invitation` says I don't have permission. Web invite shows a banner: 'SSO required'. Anyone use the CLI flow for org invites?

Tara (DevEx): Hi Jordan, welcome! We usually recommend accepting the invite in the browser first so SSO can be authorized, then you can use gh CLI. Which account did you authenticate with locally? `gh auth status` shows the account.

Jordan Lee: It showed my personal account (jordan.dev). I ran `gh auth login` again and switched to my work account (jordan@redwood.ai). After that `gh orgs accept-invitation` returned 403 with "must be authorized via SAML SSO".

Omar (Security): Org policy enforces SAML SSO and also requires org-scoped OAuth app approval for CLI tokens. If you used a PAT without SSO, GH blocks access. Try accepting invite in browser, press the blue "Authorize SSO" button on the org page, then re-run `gh auth login` in a fresh terminal.

Jordan Lee: Did that — browser invite accepted, SSO authorized, and web shows me as a member. But `gh api /user/memberships/orgs/redwood-inference` still returns role "outside_collaborator" when using the CLI token.

Tara (DevEx): Hmm, sounds like your local GH auth is still using an older token tied to the personal account. A couple of steps that usually fix it: 1) `gh auth logout --hostname github.com` then 2) `gh auth login --web` and pick the work account, 3) Ensure the token has org:read and repo scopes if prompted.

Jordan Lee: Logged out and logged back in with `--web`. `gh auth status` now shows jordan@redwood.ai. Re-ran `gh api /user/memberships/orgs/redwood-inference` and it now returns "member". Clone works. Thanks.

IT Bot: Reminder: Org requires 2FA. If you haven't enabled it, verify at https://github.com/settings/security.

Jordan Lee: 2FA already on (auth app). One minor issue: my personal GH still shows my work email which I wanted to keep for some OSS stuff. Will that cause future invite collisions?

Omar (Security): To avoid collisions, remove work email from personal account or add the work email to the org invitee whitelist via DevEx. We usually remove the work email from personal accounts to keep mapping deterministic. Either is fine but removing is cleaner.

Tara (DevEx): If you want, I can nudge IT to remove any stray pending memberships. Glad the CLI flow works now — added a short note to the onboarding doc about doing SSO in the browser first.

Jordan Lee: Appreciate it. Small win for CLI users. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
